column3: The tombs of the emperors of the Western Xia, a lost kingdom of the 11th to 13th centuries, with earthen mounds rising from the desert plain at the foot of the Helan Mountains.
A ruined fort turned into a film set for Chinese movies, with mud walls that look like the Wild West.
Thousands of ancient carvings of animals, hunters and faces on the rocks of the Helan Mountains, some of them thousands of years old.
A square pagoda in the north of Yinchuan, with a long history, built about 1,600 years ago, and rebuilt many times.
A lake beside a desert near Yinchuan, with golden dunes on one side and reeds and water birds on the other.
A mosque in the city center of Yinchuan with a green dome and a minaret, a place of prayer for the Hui community.
Mutton boiled on the bone and eaten by hand with salt, simple and rich, a classic of the northwest.
Ningxia's goji berries are the best known in China, red, sweet and slightly sour, and are used in soups, teas and traditional medicine.
Wine from vineyards on the eastern slope of the Helan Mountains, where dry, sunny weather helps grapes ripen, and has won international prizes.
A hot, spicy soup of lamb organs, and is eaten at breakfast with flatbread.
A tea of eight treasures, including goji, jujube, rock sugar and dried fruit, brewed in a lidded cup, a Hui welcome.
Tender lamb from the Huangqu Bridge area, known for its mild flavor and soft texture.
Hua'er are folk songs of the northwest, sung outdoors with high, free voices about love and the landscape.
A traditional Hui wedding with prayers, feasting and special foods, where families gather to celebrate.
A desert park where a huge sand slope meets the Yellow River, with sand sliding, camel rides and a famous sand-control railway line.
A great bend of the Yellow River near Zhongwei, where the river turns and runs among green fields and desert.
A big desert with high dunes, small lakes and oases, one of the largest deserts in China.
A temple in Zhongwei that combines Buddhist, Taoist and Confucian halls under one roof.
Crisp, sweet apples grown in the sunny, dry climate of Zhongwei, with bright red skin.
Melons grown in a gravel field that keeps the soil warm and moist, with a sweet and crisp flesh.
A wetland park in Shizuishan, with reeds, lakes and many water birds in a desert landscape.
Lamb raised on the dry grasslands near Shizuishan, which is simply boiled or roasted.
A set of 108 white pagodas arranged in a triangle on a hillside above the Yellow River, with a mysterious history.
A gorge where the Yellow River runs through red cliffs, a place for boat trips.
Boiled mutton on the bone from Wuzhong, a rich local dish.
Tan sheep from Yanchi, prized for its fine, tender lamb with no gamey taste, thanks to salty grass.
Cave temples carved into a red sandstone cliff, with a giant seated Buddha about 20 meters high, from the Northern Wei to Tang dynasties.
The last big mountain crossed by the Red Army on the Long March in 1935, with green forests and a memorial park.
Buckwheat noodles from Guyuan, a high, cool area where buckwheat grows well.
